sentences.text: How? Who else has power? And did the last vote matter?
In 2020, a rule change reset his terms to zero.
Every citizen from 18 can vote, even abroad.
But here's the weird part: you vote twice.
Two ballots: one for a party, one for a local candidate.
Half the seats go to parties over 5%, half to district winners.
That's the State Duma. It makes the laws.
Now it gets strange: the upper house isn't elected.
Regions send two each, the president adds 30, and it approves every law.
The president picks the PM; the Duma says yes.
He's elected for six years: over half wins, or a run-off.
In 2026, his party won 349 seats. A liberal rival was barred.
And the gap in the timeline? Two terms in a row was the limit, so in 2008 he became PM.
Can a vote be fair if you know who wins?
